source.title: A Theory of Generalization in Deep Learning

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is provided.
record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization on modular division and presents a different, spectral-mechanism account of grokking; it does not replicate the original training recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior grokking work, but those cited results are not recorded as this study's results. The relevant new results are its modular-division comparison in Figure 4 and its delayed-generalization/mechanism presentation in Figure 8. Other experiments on PINNs, images, and preference tuning do not report grokking-like delayed generalization.
record.test_reason: The AdamW baseline repeats the Power et al. setup: modular division mod 97 at 25% training fraction with a 2-layer Transformer. Figure 4 shows training accuracy saturating early and held-out accuracy reaching 95% only at step 29,450, which bears directly on V1. The rest of the paper is theory plus the authors' own optimizer. Figure 8 is an unspecified illustration of the frozen-kernel spectral filter, not a documented experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also claim that grokking is signal migrating from the test-invisible reservoir into the signal channel as the kernel evolves. They say the frozen-kernel limit of their theory reproduces grokking from one spectral filter, calling it delayed filter resolution 'not a sudden change in optimization phase'. Their optimizer 'collapses the grokking delay' (4.9x fewer steps to 95%).
record.recipe_differences: The modular-division experiment uses a population-risk optimizer update compared with AdamW, rather than reproducing the original training recipe. The paper also presents a spectral-filter explanation.
record.method_sensitivity: On the modular-division task at 25% training fraction, the reported steps to 95% held-out accuracy differ between AdamW (29,450) and population-risk training (5,950).

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing AdamW with the authors' SNR-gated Adam variant reaches 95% held-out accuracy at step 5,950 instead of 29,450 (4.9x), with similar ratios at the 50%, 80% and 99% thresholds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The length of the grokking delay depends strongly on the optimizer's gradient signal-to-noise gating; an SNR gate on Adam shortens it about 5x.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 8 is a spectral-filter illustration: fast noise-fitting modes saturate first and slow signal modes overtake them around t≈10^5, when test accuracy rises. No model or task is specified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking as the delayed resolution of a kernel spectral filter, with signal migrating from low-mobility modes.

record.problems: The Figure 8 grokking illustration does not state the model, task, architecture, or uncertainty. The modular-division result reports a single training fraction and no uncertainty or run count for that experiment.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying grokking results left out. Other reported experiments and metrics do not measure delayed generalization.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size: only one training fraction (25%) is run.
No circuit identification, no measurement of memorizing components, and no progress measures computed on the real modular-division run.
All parts. The DPO experiment reports no delayed generalization.
Adaptive-optimizer instabilities and softmax floating-point limits are not isolated. The study's optimizer change shortens the delay but is not framed or tested as removing an artifact.

missing.what: Steps to the 50%, 80% and 99% held-out accuracy thresholds. AdamW: 28.6k / 29.1k / 29.9k. Population-risk: 5.45k / 5.7k / 6.1k.
Training-accuracy saturation step and the memorization gap (train minus test accuracy) over time, for both optimizers. Shown only graphically.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is mainly a theory paper plus an optimizer. Its only grokking experiment is one run per optimizer at a single training fraction, with no seeds or uncertainty reported for this task. The grokking account is theoretical and is not tested against mechanistic measurements in the trained Transformer.

versions.untested_parts: No training-set-size sweep is reported, so whether delay grows as the training set shrinks is untested.
The paper reports a gradual spectral transfer account, but does not identify a Fourier circuit or measure memorizing components being removed.
No grokking-delay tests varying initialization scale, weight norm, or lazy-to-rich transition on non-algorithmic data.
No delayed-generalization test during realistic LLM pretraining or ordinary fine-tuning; the Qwen experiment uses DPO on deliberately noisy preferences and reports alignment metrics, not grokking.
No test of a low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
No comparison of the identifiable algorithms learned across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.
No test of adaptive-optimizer instability, softmax floating-point limits, or whether controlling such effects removes the delay.
